Scheme: Indian Agricultural Research Institute - Scholarship

Ministry: Ministry Of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare

Department: Department of Agriculture Research and Education

Level: Central

Target beneficiaries: Individual

Overview

The Indian Agricultural Research Institute (IARI) Junior and Senior Scholarship shall be awarded to M.Sc. and Ph.D. students admitted under General Open Competition Scheme.

Detailed description

The Awards shall be made by the Dean and Joint Director (Education) of the Institute on the advice of the “Standing Committee on Scholarships Financial Assistance and Academic Progress”, which shall take into consideration the merit of

each applicant based initially on his admission and subsequently on his performance at the Post Graduate School.

Duration

The normal duration of junior scholarships for M.Sc. course will be two years and that of senior scholarships for Ph.D. course will be three years. However, on the recommendation of the Chairperson of the student and Professor of the Division based on appraisal of the progress and details of justification for the extension needed, the period of junior/senior scholarships is extendable in exceptional cases for period not exceeding three months/six months, respectively. In the case of SC/ST/PC students, the scholarships are extendable upto a period of six months/one year, respectively.

The students who have undergone introductory courses on agriculture in the first year of their study at IARI shall be provided Institute scholarship for a period of one year in addition to the provisions mentioned above.

The scholarships shall be awarded initially for a period of one academic year from the date of joining the Post Graduate School or the commencement of the academic year, whichever is later, and can be renewed for another year in the case of M.Sc. and two years in the case of Ph.D. students, subject to the earning of Overall Grade Point Average for continuing in the Post Graduate School.

Requests for extension beyond these limits will be examined by the Dean on their merits. The total period for which scholarships shall be awarded including extension period shall not exceed three years and three months in the case of M.Sc. students, and four years and six months in the case of Ph.D. students.

The payment of scholarship/fellowship should be reviewed at the end of 3rd trimester and only those students will e permitted to continue getting fellowship who maintain the OGPA of 6.50 out of 10.00 at the end of 3rd trimester. All M.Sc./ Ph.D. students will be required to maintain the minimum OGPA of 6.00 out of 10.00 at the end of 3rd trimester to continue on the Post Graduate School rolls.

The scholarship shall be paid only for the period of residence of the recipient at Post Graduate School (inclusive of the summer vacation, the trimester breaks and such other leave as may be sanctioned under the rules) upto the date of final viva-voce (i.e. till they are on the rolls), subject to the condition that the maximum period of scholarship prescribed shall in no case be extended and provided he/she continues to reside in the Post Graduate Hostel and marks his/her attendance in the concerned division.

Benefits

The value of the M.Sc. and Ph.D. scholarship will be ₹ 7,560/- and ₹ 10,500/- per month, respectively. The scholarship shall be drawn in the extension period also where such extension beyond two/three years, respectively, has been granted. The scholarship will be inclusive of all fees and other charges of the teaching institution. In addition to the monthly amount of junior/senior scholarship a contingent grant of ₹ 6,000/- per academic year for M.Sc. students, and ₹ 10,000/- per academic year for Ph.D. students will be paid towards the cost of experimental material, books, the thesis and the study tours required for the study as recommended by the Chairperson/Professor concerned.

Scholarship to the In-service Candidates/ Departmental Students

As per ICAR norms, the In-service candidates joining M.Sc./Ph.D. course on study leave/ deputation who are in receipt of study allowance/ halting allowance/deputation allowance, etc. in addition to full leave salary, the scholarship amount will be adjusted so that they will get a maximum benefit of ₹ 3,000/- p.m. only in addition to full leave salary. This is in addition to the payment of the contingent grant. Those in-service candidates who are not in receipt of JRF/SRF and receiving a partial salary (half or leave without pay) will also be eligible to get an Institute Scholarship of ₹ 3,000/- p.m. provided they are employed by ICAR/SAU system, either nominated by ICAR or selected for admission by any university and who opt to join at a place other than the one where working and provided further that the third degree is not from the same institute.

Eligibility

For the M.Sc./M.Tech. (Agricultural Engineering only) Courses:

Only those candidates who had their Bachelor’s Degree Programmes under 10+2+4 OR 10+2+3 OR 10+1+4 system (OR awarded B.Sc. degree under 10+2+2 system prior to 1985) and fulfill the qualifications as prescribed in the Information Bulletin are eligible to apply for admission.

For the Ph.D. Courses:

Candidates must have obtained at least 60% marks OR an Overall Grade Point Average (OGPA) of 7.50 out of 10.00 OR 3.75 out of 5.00 OR 3.00 out of 4.00 OR 2.25 out of 3.00 (For SC/ST/PC candidates: 55% marks OR OGPA of 7.00 out of 10.00 OR 3.50 out of 5.00 OR 2.80 out of 4.00 OR 2.10 out of 3.00) in M.Sc. / M.Tech. degree program. In no case, the conversion of OGPA into percentage will be considered for the calculation of marks where the OGPA is awarded.

The scholarships will be admissible to students of Indian Nationality as defined in the constitution of India or persons domiciled in India, irrespective of sex, race, or religion.

A fellow will devote his/her whole time to the approved study and will not be allowed to accept or hold another appointment paid or otherwise.

Age Limit

The minimum age limit for admission to Ph.D. shall be 21 years. The age shall be reckoned as of 31st July of the year of admission and no further relaxation will be given to the candidates

Application process

Online

To request an application form and the Information Bulletin, send a crossed Demand Draft for ₹ 575/- drawn in favour of the Registrar, Post Graduate School, Indian Agricultural Research Institute, New Delhi 110 012, along with a written request clearly indicating your full and legible address.

You can also purchase the application form and the Information Bulletin in person at Syndicate Bank, Pusa Campus by making a payment of ₹ 500/- (₹ 250/- for SC/ST/PC candidates plus the charges prescribed by the Bank).

You can also download the Information Bulletin, Admit Cards, Application Form, and Acknowledgement Card from the Institute website at

http://www.iari.res.in

. In this case, you must enclose a Demand Draft of ₹ 500/- (for the General/ OBC category) and ₹ 250/- (for SC/ST/PC category) along with the Application Form.

8. Caste Certificate.

Scheme: ICAR Emeritus Professor

Ministry: Ministry Of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare

Department: Department of Agriculture Research and Education

Implementing agency: Indian Council Of Agricultural Research

Level: Central

Scheme type: Centrally Sponsored Scheme

Target beneficiaries: Individual

Overview

The ICAR floated the Scheme of Emeritus Professor in order to provide an opportunity to the superannuated teachers/ Scientists of universities, colleges and institutions under ICAR-AU System.

Detailed description

The "ICAR Emeritus Professor Scheme" is implemented by the Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR), Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare, to utilise the expertise and services of outstanding superannuated teachers and scientists from the National Agricultural Research and Education System (NARES). The scheme provides an opportunity to retired professionals to undertake teaching, training, student research guidance, and other academic activities in agricultural universities and institutions. It supports the development of instructional materials, textbooks, and e-learning resources for use in national agricultural education programmes and distance education. The scheme aims to address shortages in faculty positions, strengthen agricultural education, and leverage the experience of retired experts in addressing nationally important academic and policy issues. It also encourages retired teachers and scientists to contribute to higher agricultural education, particularly in economically and ecologically underprivileged regions.

Benefits

Honorarium:

Honorarium of ₹50,000/- per month is provided to the Emeritus Professor.

Contingency Grant:

A non-lapsable contingency grant of ₹1,00,000/- per annum is provided.

The grant may be used for secretarial assistance, stationery, postage, consumables, books, journals, and travel related to the approved assignment.

The grant may also be used for attending one scientific meeting or conference within India per year.

Economy-class airfare, admissible daily allowance, and road mileage are allowed from the contingency grant.

No separate Travel Allowance (TA) or Daily Allowance (DA) is provided.

The grant is released based on requisition and actual utilization of the previous year's grant.

Books and journals purchased from the grant become the property of the concerned university or college.

The contingency grant may be enhanced with the concurrence of the Financial Adviser (Department of Agricultural Research and Education), depending on the assignment.

Academic and Institutional Support:

The Emeritus Professor is entitled to medical and other facilities available to university faculty members.

The Emeritus Professor remains attached to an Agricultural University, ICAR Deemed University, or another eligible institution that provides the required facilities.

Research and Professional Engagement

The Emeritus Professor is provided an opportunity to continue approved academic, research, and professional activities in agriculture and allied sciences.

Eligibility

The applicant should be an outstanding superannuated teacher/Scientist with a good record of published work and teaching/ training experience of a minimum of 5 years.

The maximum age limit for applying for ICAR Emeritus Professor will be 65 years.

The ICAR Emeritus Professor can work under this scheme up to the age of 70 years or up to three years, whichever is earlier.

The teacher/Professor who is to retire in the next 12 months time is eligible to apply.

The application should be submitted through the Executive Authority where the Emeritus Professor proposes to work in the prescribed Proforma to the Deputy Director General (Education), ICAR.

Note:

Preference will be given to applicants superannuated within one year from the date of notification. The notification for filling up vacant slots will be issued depending upon the vacancies from time to time. The applications received within the period specified in the circular will only be entertained.

Application process

Online

Step 1:

The applicant should ensure that he/she is a Principal Scientist, Professor, or equivalent faculty member of repute, is physically fit and mentally alert, and meets the eligibility conditions of the scheme.

Step 2:

The applicant should ensure that he/she has either up to 1 year of service remaining before retirement or has superannuated within 1 year from the last working day of the notification month.

Step 3:

The applicant should prepare the required details and documents in the prescribed application format.

Step 4:

The applicant should visit the

Research Leadership Building System (RLBS) Portal

of ICAR.

Step 5:

The applicant should complete and submit the online application through the RLBS Portal within the prescribed application period.

Step 6:

The applicant should ensure that the application is submitted only through the online mode, as applications submitted through any other mode will not be accepted.

Step 7:

The submitted application will be processed by ICAR for scrutiny and further consideration under the scheme.

Step 8:

In case of any difficulty during the online application process, the applicant may seek assistance through the designated email support provided by ICAR.

Required documents

Academic Qualification certificate/document.

Employment Record certificate/document.

Research Experience certificate/document.

Teaching Experience-Courses Taught certificate/document.

Awards & Recognitions certificate/document.

Fellowship of National/International Academics certificate/document.

Need to upload the duly signed copy of the NOC. Its is mandatory for the persons who are in service.

Application Form

Frequently asked questions

Question: What is the "ICAR Emeritus Professor Scheme"?

Answer: The ICAR Emeritus Professor Scheme is an initiative of the Indian Council of Agricultural Research to utilise the expertise of outstanding retired teachers and scientists for teaching, training, research guidance, and academic activities in agricultural institutions.

Question: Who implements the ICAR Emeritus Professor Scheme?

Answer: The scheme is implemented by the Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR), Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare.

Question: What is the main objective of the scheme?

Answer: The scheme aims to strengthen agricultural education by engaging experienced retired professionals in teaching, training, student guidance, and the development of educational resources.

Question: Who is eligible to apply under the scheme?

Answer: An outstanding superannuated teacher or scientist with a good record of published work and at least 5 years of teaching or training experience is eligible to apply under the scheme.

Question: What is the maximum age limit for applying?

Answer: The applicant must not be more than 65 years of age at the time of application.

Question: Can a teacher who has not yet retired apply for the scheme?

Answer: Yes, a teacher or professor who is due to retire within the next 12 months is eligible to apply under the scheme.

Question: How long can an Emeritus Professor work under the scheme?

Answer: An Emeritus Professor can work under the scheme for up to 3 years or until attaining the age of 70 years, whichever is earlier.

Question: What honorarium is provided under the scheme?

Answer: The selected Emeritus Professor receives an honorarium of ₹50,000/- per month.

Question: Is any contingency grant provided under the scheme?

Answer: Yes, a non-lapsable contingency grant of ₹1,00,000/- per annum is provided to support approved academic and professional activities.

Question: What expenses can be covered through the contingency grant?

Answer: The contingency grant can be used for secretarial assistance, stationery, postage, consumables, books, journals, travel related to the assignment, and participation in one scientific meeting or conference within India each year.

Question: Is separate Travel Allowance or Daily Allowance provided?

Answer: No, separate Travel Allowance (TA) or Daily Allowance (DA) is not provided under the scheme. Such expenses must be met from the contingency grant.

Question: Are medical facilities available to an Emeritus Professor?

Answer: Yes, the Emeritus Professor is entitled to medical and other facilities that are available to the faculty members of the host institution.

Question: Where can an Emeritus Professor undertake the approved assignment?

Answer: The Emeritus Professor may remain attached to an Agricultural University, an ICAR Deemed University, or another eligible institution that provides the required facilities.

Question: Is any preference given during the selection process?

Answer: Yes, preference is given to applicants who have superannuated within one year from the date of notification.

Question: How should an eligible applicant submit the application?

Answer: The applicant must submit the prescribed application form through the Executive Authority of the institution where the proposed work will be carried out and forward it to the Deputy Director General (Education), ICAR within the period specified in the notification.

No separate Travel Allowance (TA) or Daily Allowance (DA) is provided.

The grant is released based on requisition and actual utilization of the previous year's grant.

Books and journals purchased from the grant become the property of the concerned university or college.

The contingency grant may be enhanced with the concurrence of the Financial Adviser (Department of Agricultural Research and Education), depending on the assignment.

Academic and Institutional Support:

The Emeritus Professor is entitled to medical and other facilities available to university faculty members.

The Emeritus Professor remains attached to an Agricultural University, ICAR Deemed University, or another eligible institution that provides the required facilities.

Research and Professional Engagement

The Emeritus Professor is provided an opportunity to continue approved academic, research, and professional activities in agriculture and allied sciences.

Eligibility

The applicant should be an outstanding superannuated teacher/Scientist with a good record of published work and teaching/ training experience of a minimum of 5 years.

The maximum age limit for applying for ICAR Emeritus Professor will be 65 years.

The ICAR Emeritus Professor can work under this scheme up to the age of 70 years or up to three years, whichever is earlier.

The teacher/Professor who is to retire in the next 12 months time is eligible to apply.

The application should be submitted through the Executive Authority where the Emeritus Professor proposes to work in the prescribed Proforma to the Deputy Director General (Education), ICAR.

Note:

Preference will be given to applicants superannuated within one year from the date of notification. The notification for filling up vacant slots will be issued depending upon the vacancies from time to time. The applications received within the period specified in the circular will only be entertained.

Application process

Online

Step 1:

The applicant should ensure that he/she is a Principal Scientist, Professor, or equivalent faculty member of repute, is physically fit and mentally alert, and meets the eligibility conditions of the scheme.

Step 2:

The applicant should ensure that he/she has either up to 1 year of service remaining before retirement or has superannuated within 1 year from the last working day of the notification month.

Step 3:

The applicant should prepare the required details and documents in the prescribed application format.

Step 4:

The applicant should visit the

Research Leadership Building System (RLBS) Portal

of ICAR.

Step 5:

The applicant should complete and submit the online application through the RLBS Portal within the prescribed application period.

Step 6:

The applicant should ensure that the application is submitted only through the online mode, as applications submitted through any other mode will not be accepted.

Step 7:

The submitted application will be processed by ICAR for scrutiny and further consideration under the scheme.

Step 8:

In case of any difficulty during the online application process, the applicant may seek assistance through the designated email support provided by ICAR.

Required documents

Academic Qualification certificate/document.

Employment Record certificate/document.

Research Experience certificate/document.

Teaching Experience-Courses Taught certificate/document.

Awards & Recognitions certificate/document.

Fellowship of National/International Academics certificate/document.

Need to upload the duly signed copy of the NOC. Its is mandatory for the persons who are in service.

Application Form

Frequently asked questions

Question: What is the "ICAR Emeritus Professor Scheme"?

Answer: The ICAR Emeritus Professor Scheme is an initiative of the Indian Council of Agricultural Research to utilise the expertise of outstanding retired teachers and scientists for teaching, training, research guidance, and academic activities in agricultural institutions.

Question: Who implements the ICAR Emeritus Professor Scheme?

Answer: The scheme is implemented by the Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR), Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare.

Question: What is the main objective of the scheme?

Answer: The scheme aims to strengthen agricultural education by engaging experienced retired professionals in teaching, training, student guidance, and the development of educational resources.

Question: Who is eligible to apply under the scheme?

Answer: An outstanding superannuated teacher or scientist with a good record of published work and at least 5 years of teaching or training experience is eligible to apply under the scheme.

Question: What is the maximum age limit for applying?

Answer: The applicant must not be more than 65 years of age at the time of application.

Question: Can a teacher who has not yet retired apply for the scheme?

Answer: Yes, a teacher or professor who is due to retire within the next 12 months is eligible to apply under the scheme.

Question: How long can an Emeritus Professor work under the scheme?

Answer: An Emeritus Professor can work under the scheme for up to 3 years or until attaining the age of 70 years, whichever is earlier.

Question: What honorarium is provided under the scheme?

Answer: The selected Emeritus Professor receives an honorarium of ₹50,000/- per month.

Question: Is any contingency grant provided under the scheme?

Answer: Yes, a non-lapsable contingency grant of ₹1,00,000/- per annum is provided to support approved academic and professional activities.

Question: What expenses can be covered through the contingency grant?

Answer: The contingency grant can be used for secretarial assistance, stationery, postage, consumables, books, journals, travel related to the assignment, and participation in one scientific meeting or conference within India each year.

Question: Is separate Travel Allowance or Daily Allowance provided?

Answer: No, separate Travel Allowance (TA) or Daily Allowance (DA) is not provided under the scheme. Such expenses must be met from the contingency grant.

Question: Are medical facilities available to an Emeritus Professor?

Answer: Yes, the Emeritus Professor is entitled to medical and other facilities that are available to the faculty members of the host institution.

Question: Where can an Emeritus Professor undertake the approved assignment?

Answer: The Emeritus Professor may remain attached to an Agricultural University, an ICAR Deemed University, or another eligible institution that provides the required facilities.

Question: Is any preference given during the selection process?

Answer: Yes, preference is given to applicants who have superannuated within one year from the date of notification.

Question: How should an eligible applicant submit the application?

Answer: The applicant must submit the prescribed application form through the Executive Authority of the institution where the proposed work will be carried out and forward it to the Deputy Director General (Education), ICAR within the period specified in the notification.

Scheme: ICAR Emeritus Scientist Scheme

Ministry: Ministry Of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare

Department: Department of Agriculture Research and Education

Implementing agency: Indian Council Of Agricultural Research

Level: Central

Scheme type: Centrally Sponsored Scheme

Target beneficiaries: Individual

Overview

The scheme aims to utilize the expertise of outstanding superannuated scientists of the National Agricultural Research System by supporting nationally important research, teaching, human resource development, and extension activities through honorarium and research grants.

Detailed description

The "ICAR Emeritus Scientist" scheme is implemented by the Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR), Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare to utilize the services of outstanding superannuated scientists for completing nationally important research work and contributing to agricultural education and development. The scheme supports retired scientists in continuing ongoing research projects of national importance and participating in specialized teaching programmes. It also promotes the development of instructional materials and addresses policy issues related to agriculture and allied sciences. The scheme provides financial assistance in the form of honorarium, contingency grants, and support for research personnel. The appointment is granted for a fixed tenure of 3 years without extension.

Benefits

Honorarium:

₹50,000/- per month honorarium in addition to pension.

Subject to provisions of the Income Tax Act.

Contingency Grant:

Up to ₹2,00,000/- per annum per scientist.

Used for chemicals, glassware, books, stationery, laboratory assistance, and ministerial help.

May be enhanced with approval based on the nature of research work.

Can be used for domestic travel related to research, data collection, scientific meetings, conferences, and ICAR review meetings.

Includes economy-class airfare, eligible daily allowance, and road mileage within India.

Research Personnel Support:

Financial assistance for engagement of:

Junior Research Fellow (JRF)

Senior Research Fellow (SRF)

Research Associate (RA)

Appointment remains valid until completion of the project.

Leave Benefits:

1 month leave with honorarium for each completed year of tenure.

Leave on a pro-rata basis for any fraction of a year.

Up to 3 months leave without honorarium may be granted on health grounds with a medical certificate.

Research and Academic Support:

Opportunity to complete ongoing nationally important research.

Opportunity to teach specialized courses in universities and institutions.

Opportunity to develop instructional and multimedia educational materials.

Eligibility

The applicant must be a scientist of repute from the National Agricultural Research System (NARS).

The applicant must hold or have held the position of Principal Scientist, Professor, or above in an eligible institution.

The applicant must be retiring within the next 12 months or must have retired within 1 year from the last working day of the notification month.

The applicant must not be more than 65 years of age at the time of application.

The applicant must have at least 5 research papers published in refereed journals during the last 5 years, or must have received a national/international award or recognition.

In the case of teachers, the applicant must have received a teaching excellence award or appreciation for outstanding teaching performance.

The applicant must submit a project of national importance that is a continuation of his/her previous work.

The applicant must demonstrate that an equally competent regular scientist is not available in the institution to undertake the proposed work.

The applicant must be willing to devote full time to the approved project and must not accept any other remunerative employment during the tenure.

The applicant must not receive financial assistance for the same work from any other source while availing benefits under this scheme.

Application process

Online

Step 1:

Obtain and fill out the prescribed

application proforma

for the ICAR Emeritus Scientist Scheme.

Step 2:

Prepare the project proposal and attach all required supporting documents.

Step 3:

Submit the completed application to the Executive Authority of the institution where the proposed research, teaching, human resource development, or extension work will be carried out.

Step 4:

Obtain recommendation and justification from the Executive Authority. Only applications forwarded through the Executive Authority will be considered.

Step 5:

Email the duly recommended application to adg.hrd.applications@gmail.com.

Step 6:

Mention "Application for Emeritus Scientist Scheme – Name of Applicant – Contact Number" in the subject line of the email.

Step 7:

Ensure that the application is submitted on or before 30 March 2026.

Step 8:

The submitted application will be scrutinised and considered for selection as per the scheme guidelines.

Procedure of Selection:

The applications received will be referred to the concerned Subject Matter Division of ICAR and to a specialist in the discipline of the applicant for comments. The applications along with these comments will be placed before the Selection cum Standing Committee.

Following criteria will be taken into consideration for the selection of an Emeritus Scientist:

The scientist should have a minimum of 5 research papers in refereed journals in the last five years or should have received a national/ international level award/recognition or in case of teachers must have received national/university level awards for excellence in teaching or have received a letter of appreciation for excellence in teaching based on alumni feedback.

The project proposal is of national importance and other equally competent regular scientists are not available in the institute to carry out the proposed work.

The project proposal is in continuation of his/her work.

Required documents

The following details should be furnished with the application:

Date of superannuation/likely superannuation

Post from which superannuated/likely to superannuate

Last salary drawn/to be drawn

Employment record from the date occupying Professor/Principal Scientist or equivalent position

(Total Years)

Special assignments/international exposures /Trainings under gone:

Major scientific achievements:

Best ten Research publication of the career along with their NAAS ratings (6 & above):

Brief account of teaching and research done during the preceding 5 years:

Research Publications for the last five years along with their NAAS ratings:

Honours/Awards/Recognitions received:

Transferable technologies developed:

Success stories, if any

Frequently asked questions

Question: What is the "ICAR Emeritus Scientist Scheme"?

Answer: The ICAR Emeritus Scientist Scheme supports outstanding retired scientists in continuing nationally important research, teaching, human resource development, and extension activities in agriculture and allied sciences.

Question: Who implements this scheme?

Answer: The scheme is implemented by the Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR), Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare.

Question: Who is eligible to apply under the scheme?

Answer: Scientists of repute at the level of Principal Scientist, Professor, or above from institutions under the National Agricultural Research System are eligible to apply.

Question: What is the maximum age limit for applying?

Answer: The applicant must not be more than 65 years of age at the time of application.

Question: Can a scientist apply before retirement?

Answer: Yes, a scientist who is due to retire within the next 12 months may apply under the scheme.

Question: Can a retired scientist apply under the scheme?

Answer: Yes, a scientist who has superannuated within 1 year from the last working day of the notification month may apply.

Question: What financial assistance is provided under the scheme?

Answer: The selected Emeritus Scientist receives an honorarium of ₹50,000/- per month along with contingency and research support grants.

Question: Is a contingency grant available under the scheme?

Answer: Yes, a contingency grant of up to ₹2,00,000/- per annum may be provided to meet approved research-related expenses.

Question: Can the contingency grant be used for travel?

Answer: Yes, the contingency grant may be used for approved domestic travel related to research work, scientific meetings, conferences, and review meetings.

Question: Is support available for engaging research personnel?

Answer: Yes, financial assistance may be provided for engaging a Junior Research Fellow, Senior Research Fellow, or Research Associate for the approved project.

Question: Can an Emeritus Scientist undertake another job during the tenure?

Answer: No, the Emeritus Scientist must devote full time to the approved project and cannot accept any regular or part-time remunerative employment during the tenure.

Question: What is the duration of the appointment under the scheme?

Answer: The appointment is granted for a period of 3 years.

Question: Can the tenure be extended after completion of 3 years?

Answer: No, no extension is granted beyond the approved tenure of 3 years.

Question: Where should the application be submitted?

Answer: The application must be submitted through the Executive Authority of the concerned institution and emailed to the designated ICAR email address.

Question: What happens if the Emeritus Scientist accepts another employment during the project period?

Answer: The project will be terminated from the date the Emeritus Scientist accepts another position or employment.

Scheme: ICAR Junior Research Fellowship For Post-Graduate Studies In Agricultural Sciences

Ministry: Ministry Of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare

Department: Department of Agriculture Research and Education

Implementing agency: Indian Council Of Agricultural Research

Level: Central

Scheme type: Central Sector Scheme

Target beneficiaries: Individual

Overview

ICAR awards a certain number of Junior Research Fellowships for Postgraduate Studies (course and research work) leading to a Master’s degree, in different disciplines of agriculture and allied sciences. This is done to encourage talented students to undertake higher agricultural education.

Detailed description

ICAR awards a certain number of Junior Research Fellowships for Postgraduate Studies (course and research work) leading to a Master’s degree, in different disciplines of agriculture and allied sciences. This is done to ensure the recognition of talent and promotion of merit in general, and for encouraging talented students to undertake higher agricultural education. The duration of the fellowship is two years. The minimum age limit shall be 19 years as of the date of the examination. Reservation of various categories such as SC/ST/OBC and PH etc will be given as per Government of India rules/instructions issued from time to time.

Benefits

Veterinary Sciences:

₹ 12,000/- per month With a contingency grant of ₹ 6,000/- per annum.

All disciplines other than Veterinary Sciences:

₹ 8,640/- per month With a contingency grant of ₹ 6,000/- per annum.

The rates of fellowship and contingency grants for higher studies will be as prescribed by the Council from time to time.

Eligibility

Method of Award:

ICAR-JRF (PGS) will be awarded on the basis of merit in the All India Competitive Entrance Examination for

(i) ICAR-JRF (PGS), and

(ii) concurrent admission to Master’s degree program at

a) State Agricultural Universities (SAUs), and

b) Deemed Universities viz. IARI (New Delhi) / IVRI (Izatnagar) / NDRI (Karnal) / CIFE (Mumbai) / AAU (Allahabad), Central Agricultural University (Imphal, Manipur), and

c) Central Universities having faculty of agriculture viz. Banaras Hindu University (BHU), Aligarh Muslim University (AMU), Visva Bharti, and Nagaland University, collectively hereinafter referred to as the Agricultural Universities (AUs).

Only those candidates having passed their Bachelor’s Degree or appearing at the Final Examination of the Bachelor’s Degree in the concerned field, under 10+2+5, 10+2+4 or 10+2+3 (only for basic science subjects) are eligible to apply for admission. (For admission, the eligibility requirement laid down by the respective AUs including remedial courses and tenure will be treated as final.)

Candidates must have obtained 60% marks or an Overall Grade Point Average (OGPA) of 6.60/10.00 or 3.25/5.00 or 2.6/4.00 for General, OBC, and Under Privileged States(UPS) categories whereas, for SC/ST/Physically Handicapped (PH) categories, the candidates must have obtained 55% marks or an OGPA of 5.5/10.00 or 2.75/5.00 or 2.20/4.00. The equivalence of OGPA to percent marks, where needed, will be certified by the Registrar of the concerned University

For admission in M.V.Sc., candidates must have completed B.V.Sc.&A.H. with internship before the date of registration in the University.

The minimum age limit shall be 19 years as of the date of the examination. No relaxation is admissible regarding the minimum age limit.

Note 1:

Reservation of various categories such as SC/ST/OBC and PH etc. will be given as per Government of India rules/instructions issued from time to time. The responsibility of verification of the genuineness of SC/ST/OBC and PH certificates will solely rest with the concerned Agricultural University (AU) where the candidate has been recommended for admission or granted provisional admission.

Note 2:

The ICAR-JRF (PGS) will NOT be available for admission in any university other than the AUs as mentioned above.

Application process

Offline

Step 1:

Candidates need to aррly fоr

Оnline Registrаtiоn

by using a unique Emаil Id аnd Mоbile Nо.

Step 2:

Nоw, fill in the neсessаry detаils suсh аs Рersоnаl Detаils, Соntасt Detаils, Асаdemiс Quаlifiсаtiоns, etс.

Step 3:

Uрlоаd the required documents like the sсаnned рhоtоgrарh, signаture, аnd thumb imрressiоn аfter filling uр the detаils.

Step 4:

Nоw, Раy the Аррliсаtiоn Fees.

Step 5:

Аfter filling the аррliсаtiоn fоrm, саndidаtes will get the system generаted Аррliсаtiоn Number.

Step 6:

Оn соmрleting the аbоve рrосess аррliсаnts will hаve tо send the hаrd сорy оf the оnline аррliсаtiоn аnd рrооf оf fee раyment tо the СОE (Аgril. Edn.) by роst.

Application Correction:

After submitting the application form for ICAR JRF candidates will get a chance to correct their mistakes. The NTA will provide a correction window to edit the application for the last time. With the help of credentials, candidates can update the application form and rectify their mistakes. No further chance will be given to candidates if they fail to correct their application in this window.

Required documents

Саndidаte’s Рhоtоgrарh

Саndidаte’s Signаture

Thumb Imрressiоn

Gоvt Identity Саrd Detаils like Ааdhааr Number /Eleсtiоn Саrd (EРIС Nо.)/Раssроrt number/Rаtiоn Саrd Number/ Bаnk Ассоunt Number/РАN Number/ Оther vаlid Gоvt Ids.

Three identiсаl сорies оf the lаtest раssроrt size соlоured рhоtоgrарhs (with nаme аnd dаte)

Сорy оf раyment оf аррliсаtiоn Fee (as рrооf)

Роst-оffiсe reсeiрt аs роstаl disраtсh рrооf оf аррliсаtiоn.

Аddress fоr соmmuniсаtiоn, Mоbile Number, emаil id, etс.

Bаnk Ассоunt Detаils.

Note:

The Thumb Imрressiоn used fоr filling the Оnline Аррliсаtiоn Fоrm fоr IСАR exam shоuld be Left (fоr Mаles) аnd Right (fоr Femаles).

Frequently asked questions

Question: What are different modes to apply for JRF?

Answer: Application Forms can only be submitted through online mode on the website https://icar.nta.nic.in. The Application Form other than online mode will not be accepted

Question: Can I submit two application forms for two courses at a time?

Answer: NO. Only one application is to be submitted by a candidate

Question: What documents or certificates do I need to upload along with the Application Form?

Answer: • Candidates need to upload scanned images of photographs, signatures, and thumb impressions, with the Application Form. • No certificates are required to be uploaded along with the Application Form at the time of online submission. • The documents/certificates etc., shall be verified directly at the time of admission in the admitting university.

Question: How can I pay Application Fee ?

Answer: Fee can be paid using SBI/Syndicate/HDFC Payment Gateway through Debit Card/Credit Card/Net Banking/UPI. Candidates need to keep proof of fee paid.

Question: If I have made any mistake(s) while registering/applying, can I make changes later in the Application Form ?

Answer: Once the ‘Final Submit’ button has been clicked, the candidate’s details cannot be edited/changed. However, NTA shall open the rectification window as per the schedule and Corrections in particulars of the Application Form can be incorporated on the website only during Correction Window. No corrections shall be allowed after the closure of correction window and all particulars entered by the candidate would be considered as final

Question: How will I get my admit card ?

Answer: The admit card will be uploaded on NTA website https://icar.nta.nic.in as per the schedule communicated through the website. Candidates need to check the admit card carefully for all particulars eg Roll No. Name, Subject Group, Date of Birth, Gender, Examination Centre Name, City, and Category, etc

Question: If I do not get my Admit Card, whom should I contact?

Answer: Toll free Number and email details will be displayed on the website. 0120- 6895200; Email for queries: icar@nta.ac.in

Question: Is the ICAR JRF applicable across India?

Answer: Yes, the ICAR JRF is a national-level fellowship and is applicable to eligible students across India.

Question: Why is the ICAR JRF important for students in agriculture?

Answer: The ICAR JRF is important because it provides financial support and recognition to talented students, enabling them to pursue higher education and contribute to the development of the agriculture sector.

Question: Does the fellowship cover both coursework and research activities?

Answer: Yes, the fellowship supports both academic coursework and research work as part of the Master’s degree programme.

Ministry: Ministry Of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare

Department: Department of Agriculture Research and Education

Implementing agency: Indian Council Of Agricultural Research

Level: Central

Scheme type: Central Sector Scheme

Target beneficiaries: Individual

Overview

ICAR awards a certain number of Junior Research Fellowships for Postgraduate Studies (course and research work) leading to a Master’s degree, in different disciplines of agriculture and allied sciences. This is done to encourage talented students to undertake higher agricultural education.

Detailed description

ICAR awards a certain number of Junior Research Fellowships for Postgraduate Studies (course and research work) leading to a Master’s degree, in different disciplines of agriculture and allied sciences. This is done to ensure the recognition of talent and promotion of merit in general, and for encouraging talented students to undertake higher agricultural education. The duration of the fellowship is two years. The minimum age limit shall be 19 years as of the date of the examination. Reservation of various categories such as SC/ST/OBC and PH etc will be given as per Government of India rules/instructions issued from time to time.

Benefits

Veterinary Sciences:

₹ 12,000/- per month With a contingency grant of ₹ 6,000/- per annum.

All disciplines other than Veterinary Sciences:

₹ 8,640/- per month With a contingency grant of ₹ 6,000/- per annum.

The rates of fellowship and contingency grants for higher studies will be as prescribed by the Council from time to time.

Eligibility

Method of Award:

ICAR-JRF (PGS) will be awarded on the basis of merit in the All India Competitive Entrance Examination for

(i) ICAR-JRF (PGS), and

(ii) concurrent admission to Master’s degree program at

a) State Agricultural Universities (SAUs), and

b) Deemed Universities viz. IARI (New Delhi) / IVRI (Izatnagar) / NDRI (Karnal) / CIFE (Mumbai) / AAU (Allahabad), Central Agricultural University (Imphal, Manipur), and

c) Central Universities having faculty of agriculture viz. Banaras Hindu University (BHU), Aligarh Muslim University (AMU), Visva Bharti, and Nagaland University, collectively hereinafter referred to as the Agricultural Universities (AUs).

Only those candidates having passed their Bachelor’s Degree or appearing at the Final Examination of the Bachelor’s Degree in the concerned field, under 10+2+5, 10+2+4 or 10+2+3 (only for basic science subjects) are eligible to apply for admission. (For admission, the eligibility requirement laid down by the respective AUs including remedial courses and tenure will be treated as final.)

Candidates must have obtained 60% marks or an Overall Grade Point Average (OGPA) of 6.60/10.00 or 3.25/5.00 or 2.6/4.00 for General, OBC, and Under Privileged States(UPS) categories whereas, for SC/ST/Physically Handicapped (PH) categories, the candidates must have obtained 55% marks or an OGPA of 5.5/10.00 or 2.75/5.00 or 2.20/4.00. The equivalence of OGPA to percent marks, where needed, will be certified by the Registrar of the concerned University

For admission in M.V.Sc., candidates must have completed B.V.Sc.&A.H. with internship before the date of registration in the University.

The minimum age limit shall be 19 years as of the date of the examination. No relaxation is admissible regarding the minimum age limit.

Note 1:

Reservation of various categories such as SC/ST/OBC and PH etc. will be given as per Government of India rules/instructions issued from time to time. The responsibility of verification of the genuineness of SC/ST/OBC and PH certificates will solely rest with the concerned Agricultural University (AU) where the candidate has been recommended for admission or granted provisional admission.

Note 2:

The ICAR-JRF (PGS) will NOT be available for admission in any university other than the AUs as mentioned above.

Candidates need to aррly fоr

Оnline Registrаtiоn

by using a unique Emаil Id аnd Mоbile Nо.

Nоw, fill in the neсessаry detаils suсh аs Рersоnаl Detаils, Соntасt Detаils, Асаdemiс Quаlifiсаtiоns, etс.

Step 3:

Uрlоаd the required documents like the sсаnned рhоtоgrарh, signаture, аnd thumb imрressiоn аfter filling uр the detаils.

Step 4:

Nоw, Раy the Аррliсаtiоn Fees.

Step 5:

Аfter filling the аррliсаtiоn fоrm, саndidаtes will get the system generаted Аррliсаtiоn Number.

Step 6:

Оn соmрleting the аbоve рrосess аррliсаnts will hаve tо send the hаrd сорy оf the оnline аррliсаtiоn аnd рrооf оf fee раyment tо the СОE (Аgril. Edn.) by роst.

With the help of credentials, candidates can update the application form and rectify their mistakes. No further chance will be given to candidates if they fail to correct their application in this window.

Саndidаte’s Signаture

Three identiсаl сорies оf the lаtest раssроrt size соlоured рhоtоgrарhs (with nаme аnd dаte)

Сорy оf раyment оf аррliсаtiоn Fee (as рrооf)

Роst-оffiсe reсeiрt аs роstаl disраtсh рrооf оf аррliсаtiоn.

Аddress fоr соmmuniсаtiоn, Mоbile Number, emаil id, etс.

The Thumb Imрressiоn used fоr filling the Оnline Аррliсаtiоn Fоrm fоr IСАR exam shоuld be Left (fоr Mаles) аnd Right (fоr Femаles).

Frequently asked questions

Question: What are different modes to apply for JRF?

Answer: Application Forms can only be submitted through online mode on the website https://icar.nta.nic.in. The Application Form other than online mode will not be accepted

Question: Can I submit two application forms for two courses at a time?

Answer: NO. Only one application is to be submitted by a candidate

Question: What documents or certificates do I need to upload along with the Application Form?

Answer: • Candidates need to upload scanned images of photographs, signatures, and thumb impressions, with the Application Form. • No certificates are required to be uploaded along with the Application Form at the time of online submission. • The documents/certificates etc., shall be verified directly at the time of admission in the admitting university.

Question: How can I pay Application Fee ?

Answer: Fee can be paid using SBI/Syndicate/HDFC Payment Gateway through Debit Card/Credit Card/Net Banking/UPI. Candidates need to keep proof of fee paid.

Question: If I have made any mistake(s) while registering/applying, can I make changes later in the Application Form ?

Answer: Once the ‘Final Submit’ button has been clicked, the candidate’s details cannot be edited/changed. However, NTA shall open the rectification window as per the schedule and Corrections in particulars of the Application Form can be incorporated on the website only during Correction Window. No corrections shall be allowed after the closure of correction window and all particulars entered by the candidate would be considered as final

Question: How will I get my admit card ?

Answer: The admit card will be uploaded on NTA website https://icar.nta.nic.in as per the schedule communicated through the website. Candidates need to check the admit card carefully for all particulars eg Roll No. Name, Subject Group, Date of Birth, Gender, Examination Centre Name, City, and Category, etc

Question: If I do not get my Admit Card, whom should I contact?

Answer: Toll free Number and email details will be displayed on the website. 0120- 6895200; Email for queries: icar@nta.ac.in

Question: Is the ICAR JRF applicable across India?

Answer: Yes, the ICAR JRF is a national-level fellowship and is applicable to eligible students across India.

Question: Why is the ICAR JRF important for students in agriculture?

Answer: The ICAR JRF is important because it provides financial support and recognition to talented students, enabling them to pursue higher education and contribute to the development of the agriculture sector.

Question: Does the fellowship cover both coursework and research activities?

Answer: Yes, the fellowship supports both academic coursework and research work as part of the Master’s degree programme.

Scheme: ICAR - Post Matric Scholarship for Scheduled Caste / Scheduled Tribes Candidates

Ministry: Ministry Of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare

Department: Department of Agriculture Research and Education

Implementing agency: Indian Council Of Agricultural Research

Level: Central

Scheme type: Central Sector Scheme

Target beneficiaries: Individual

Overview

The scheme aims to provide Post-Matric Scholarship to Scheduled Castes/ Scheduled Tribes candidates for study at Bachelor Degree programme in various branches of Agriculture, viz. B.Sc. (Agri.), B.V.Sc., B.Sc. (Agril. Engg.), B.Sc. (Home Science), B.F.Sc., B.Sc. (Forestry) etc.

Detailed description

The scheme "Post Matric Scholarship for Scheduled Caste/ Scheduled Tribes Candidates" is implemented by the Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR), Department of Agricultural Research and Education (DARE), Government of India. The scheme aims to provide Post-Matric Scholarship to Scheduled Castes/ Scheduled Tribes candidates for study at Bachelor Degree programme in various branches of Agriculture, viz. B.Sc. (Agri.), B.V.Sc., B.Sc. (Agril. Engg.), B.Sc. (Home Science), B.F.Sc., B.Sc. (Forestry) etc. It is expected that through this scheme the students from the weaker sections of the society will be able to come up to receive post-graduate education in agriculture and allied sciences.

Benefits

Value Of Scholarship

The value of the scholarship will be ₹ 1,000/- per month along with a contingent grant of ₹ 750/- per annum for the payment of tuition fees, purchase of books, cost of uniforms, etc.

Duration Of Scholarship

The duration of the scholarship will cover the whole of the normal period of the particular degree programme to which the candidate is admitted.

Eligibility

The applicant must be a citizen of India.

The applicant must belong to Scheduled Castes / Scheduled Tribes communities as defined by the Government of India.

Only those students who have been admitted in Agricultural Universities in any of the undergraduate degree programmes of Agriculture & Allied Sciences will be eligible for this scholarship.

General Condition:

(a) The student who accepts this scholarship will not be permitted to avail any other scholarship / concession provided by any other agencies nor permitted to accept any part-time employment.

(b) Termination of Scholarship: The scholarship will be terminated without notice

(i) from the date the scholar debases to be on the roll of the institution or on the date of expiry of the sanction of the scholarship which ever is earlier. The scholarship can also be terminated without notice at any time if in the opinion of the institution and the Council the scholar is found to be negligent in his/her studies or is guilty of misconduct;

(ii) if the scholar is dropped by the institution due to peer performance.

Application process

Offline

Step 1:

The scholarship amount as well as the contingent grant will be remitted to the respective institutions by the Council based on the demand received from each institution through the Registrar / Comptroller of the University in the prescribed

proforma

Step 2:

The students will be eligible to receive scholarships and contingent grants from the date of joining the course.

Procedure of Selection:

The scheme provides for the award of 240 scholarships every year. These scholarships will be earmarked for individual Agricultural Universities in proportion to the actual number of scheduled castes / scheduled tribes candidates admitted.

A tentative distribution of scholarships will first be made to various agricultural universities on the basis of seats reserved by the individual agricultural universities for SC/ST candidates.

The actual number of scholarship allotted to the universities every year would, however, be determined on the basis of actual SC/ST students admitted so as to maintain approximately equal proportion between the number of SC/ST students admitted in each university to the number of scholarships available.

Payment of Scholarship

(a) The students will be eligible to receive scholarship and contingent grant from the date of joining the course.

(b) The scholarship amount as well as the contingent grant will be remitted to the respective institutions by the Council on the basis of the demand received from each institution through the Registrar / Comptroller of the University in the prescribed proforma.

(c) Scholarship during the leave on medical grounds will be admissible as follows:

Full scholarship will be paid if the absence does not exceed two months due to illness supported by medical certificate as prescribed by the concerned university.

Half the scholarship will be paid if the absence exceeds two months but not four months. The first two months scholarship will be paid on full rates and the half scholarship will be paid on full rates and the half scholarship will be paid for the preceding two months.

No scholarship will be given if the absence exceeds four months. The payment of scholarship for the first four months, however, will be governed by the sub-clause (1) and (2) above.

In the case of married women, the scholarship will be admissible at full rates upto three months absence on grounds of maternity. However, no scholarship will be paid for the period exceeding three months.

In all the above cases (sub-clause 1 to 4), the scholarship at the rates indicated will be paid only if the Head of the Institution recommends the application of the students and certifies that the scholar is likely to make up the deficiency in studies subsequently.

All these concessions indicated above in clause (1) to (4) will be available only once in the whole duration of the course.

(d) Normally, the scholarship will be continued from year to year provided the student makes satisfactory progress as prescribed by the University. However, in case the student fees on academic probation, the scholarship for the period of academic probation will be paid only at half the rates. This concession will, however, be available for one time only during the entire duration. If the student goes on academic probation for a second time during the period of the course. He will not receive any scholarship for the period of academic probation.

Required documents

Student Photo

Aadhaar Number

Caste Certificate

Details of the Aadhaar Linked Bank Account

Residential/Domicile Certificate

Proof of Admission

Proof of Identity

Marksheets of the Previous Qualified Examination

Frequently asked questions

Question: Who is eligible for this scholarship?

Answer: Students belonging to SC/ST communities, as defined by the Government of India, who are admitted to agricultural universities are eligible.

Question: Which courses are covered under this scheme?

Answer: The scholarship is available for undergraduate courses such as: B.Sc. (Agriculture) B.V.Sc. B.Sc. (Agricultural Engineering) B.Sc. (Home Science) B.F.Sc. B.Sc. (Forestry)

Question: Are students from other categories eligible?

Answer: No, this scholarship is exclusively meant for SC/ST students.

Question: What is the amount of scholarship provided?

Answer: Students receive ₹1000/- per month as scholarship.

Question: What is the duration of the scholarship?

Answer: The scholarship is provided for the entire normal duration of the degree programme.

Question: How many scholarships are awarded every year?

Answer: A total of 240 scholarships are awarded annually.

Question: How are scholarships distributed among universities?

Answer: Scholarships are allocated to agricultural universities based on the number of SC/ST students admitted.

Question: When does the scholarship payment start?

Answer: The scholarship is payable from the date the student joins the course.

Question: How is the scholarship amount disbursed?

Answer: The amount is transferred to the institution, which then disburses it to students based on official demand submissions.

Scheme: ICAR Senior Research Fellowship For Post-Graduate Studies In Agricultural Sciences

Ministry: Ministry Of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare

Department: Department of Agriculture Research and Education

Implementing agency: Indian Council Of Agricultural Research

Level: Central

Scheme type: Central Sector Scheme

Target beneficiaries: Individual

Overview

ICAR awards a certain number of Senior Research Fellowships for Ph.D. in an Agricultural University (AU), in different disciplines of agriculture and allied sciences. This is done to encourage talented students to undertake higher agricultural education.

Detailed description

In order to address the emerging challenges of agricultural research and education, the ICAR supports specific time-bound schemes/projects. The schemes/projects generally have provisions for time-bound/non-regular/ contractual engagement of manpower, contingencies, and limited need-based traveling allowance (TA), besides other specifically needed provisions for a particular scheme/project. In supersession of all previous guidelines, the following guidelines are formulated to regulate all aspects relating to engagement, emoluments, and terms and conditions of Senior Research Fellows and Research Associates working in ICAR schemes.

Benefits

Veterinary Sciences:

₹ 12,000/- per month With a contingency grant of ₹ 6,000/- per annum.

All disciplines other than Veterinary Sciences:

₹ 8,640/- per month With a contingency grant of ₹ 6,000/- per annum.

The rates of fellowship and contingency grants for higher studies will be as prescribed by the Council from time to time.

Eligibility

Method of Award

ICAR-SRF (PGS) will be awarded on the basis of merit in the All India Competitive Entrance Examination for

(i) ICAR-SRF (PGS), and

(ii) concurrent admission to Master’s degree program at

a) State Agricultural Universities (SAUs), and

b) Deemed Universities viz. IARI (New Delhi) / IVRI (Izatnagar) / NDRI (Karnal) / CIFE (Mumbai) / AAU (Allahabad), Central Agricultural University (Imphal, Manipur), and

c) Central Universities having faculty of agriculture viz. Banaras Hindu University (BHU), Aligarh Muslim University (AMU), Visva Bharti, and Nagaland University, collectively hereinafter referred to as the Agricultural Universities (AUs).

Candidates having completed their Master’s degree program with a minimum of 55% marks or an OGPA of 5.5/10.00 or 2.75/5.00 or 2.20/4.00 or an equivalent OGPA from any recognized University in India and abroad would be eligible. For SC/ST and Physically Handicapped (PH) candidates, the minimum percentage of marks will be relaxed by 5 percent or an equivalent OGPA. The equivalence of OGPA to percent marks, where needed, will be certified by the Registrar of the concerned University. Candidates appearing in the final semester would also be eligible provided they complete their postgraduate degree in all respects by the date of examination and produce the complete degree certificate from the Registrar to this effect.

The fellowship would be granted only when the candidate gets eventually admitted and pursues a Ph.D. degree in an Agricultural University(AU) other than the Agricultural University(AU) from where the candidate has completed M.Sc./M.V.Sc./ M.E./M.Tech. degree.

The upper age limit would be 30 years as of the date of the examination. For SC/ST & PH categories, the upper age limit will be relaxed by 5 years. For OBC the upper age limit will be relaxed by 3 years. For in-service candidates of Agricultural Universities (AU), the upper age limit would be 45 years as of the date of examination whereas, the academic performance requirement would remain as stated above.

NOTE 1:

Reservation of various categories such as SC/ST/OBC and PH etc. will be given as per Government of India rules/instructions issued from time to time. The responsibility of verification of the genuineness of SC/ST/OBC and PH certificates will solely rest with the concerned Agricultural University (AU) where the candidate has been recommended for admission or granted provisional admission.

NOTE 2:

The ICAR-SRF (PGS) will NOT be available for admission in any university other than the AUs as mentioned above.

Online

Nоw, fill in the neсessаry detаils suсh аs Рersоnаl Detаils, Соntасt Detаils, Асаdemiс Quаlifiсаtiоns, etс.

Step 3:

Uрlоаd the required documents like the sсаnned рhоtоgrарh, signаture, аnd thumb imрressiоn аfter filling uр the detаils.

Step 4:

Nоw, Раy the Аррliсаtiоn Fees.

Step 5:

Аfter filling the аррliсаtiоn fоrm, саndidаtes will get the system generаted Аррliсаtiоn Number.

Step 6:

Оn соmрleting the аbоve рrосess аррliсаnts will hаve tо send the hаrd сорy оf the оnline аррliсаtiоn аnd рrооf оf fee раyment tо the СОE (Аgril. Edn.) by роst.

Application Correction

After submitting the application form for ICAR SRF candidates will get a chance to correct their mistakes. The NTA will provide a correction window to edit the application for the last time. With the help of credentials, candidates can update the application form and rectify their mistakes. No further chance will be given to candidates if they fail to correct their application in this window.

Required documents

Candidates must be ready with the following documents while filling out the Application form.

Candidate’s Photograph (file size: 10 kb - 200 kb)

Candidate’s Signature (file size: 4kb - 30kb)

Thumb impression (file size: 3kb-30kb)

Govt Identity Details like Aadhaar Number /Election Card (EPIC No.)/Passport number/Ration Card Number/ Bank Account Number/PAN Number/ Other valid Govt Ids.

Three identical copies of the latest passport-size colored photographs (with name and date)

Copy of payment of application fee (As proof)

Post-office receipt as postal dispatch proof of application.

Address for communication, Mobile Number, email id, etc

Bank Account details for payment of Fee, for uploading as part of the submission of the online application.

Note - The Thumb Impression used for filling the Online Application Form for ICAR, should be Left (for Males) and Right (for Females),

Frequently asked questions

Question: Does ICAR release the application forms for PhD courses?

Answer: The National Testing Agency (NTA) conducted ICAR AICE and ICAR AIEEA on behalf of ICAR. Candidates had to visit the official website of ICAR-NTA to apply online

Question: What are different modes to apply for SRF(PhD)]?

Answer: Application Forms can only be submitted online mode on the website https://icar.nta.ac.in. The Application Form other than online mode will not be accepted

Question: Can a person submit more than one application form for the exam

Answer: NO. Only ONE application is to be submitted by a candidate for appearing in the exam.

Answer: Candidates need to upload scanned images of their photograph, signature and thumb impression, with the Application Form. No certificates are required to be uploaded along with the Application Form at the time of online submission

Scheme: ICAR Senior Research Fellowship For Post-Graduate Studies In Agricultural Sciences

Ministry: Ministry Of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare

Department: Department of Agriculture Research and Education

Implementing agency: Indian Council Of Agricultural Research

Level: Central

Scheme type: Central Sector Scheme

Target beneficiaries: Individual

Overview

ICAR awards a certain number of Senior Research Fellowships for Ph.D. in an Agricultural University (AU), in different disciplines of agriculture and allied sciences. This is done to encourage talented students to undertake higher agricultural education.

Detailed description

In order to address the emerging challenges of agricultural research and education, the ICAR supports specific time-bound schemes/projects. The schemes/projects generally have provisions for time-bound/non-regular/ contractual engagement of manpower, contingencies, and limited need-based traveling allowance (TA), besides other specifically needed provisions for a particular scheme/project. In supersession of all previous guidelines, the following guidelines are formulated to regulate all aspects relating to engagement, emoluments, and terms and conditions of Senior Research Fellows and Research Associates working in ICAR schemes.

Benefits

Veterinary Sciences:

₹ 12,000/- per month With a contingency grant of ₹ 6,000/- per annum.

All disciplines other than Veterinary Sciences:

₹ 8,640/- per month With a contingency grant of ₹ 6,000/- per annum.

The rates of fellowship and contingency grants for higher studies will be as prescribed by the Council from time to time.

Eligibility

Method of Award

ICAR-SRF (PGS) will be awarded on the basis of merit in the All India Competitive Entrance Examination for

(i) ICAR-SRF (PGS), and

(ii) concurrent admission to Master’s degree program at

a) State Agricultural Universities (SAUs), and

b) Deemed Universities viz. IARI (New Delhi) / IVRI (Izatnagar) / NDRI (Karnal) / CIFE (Mumbai) / AAU (Allahabad), Central Agricultural University (Imphal, Manipur), and

c) Central Universities having faculty of agriculture viz. Banaras Hindu University (BHU), Aligarh Muslim University (AMU), Visva Bharti, and Nagaland University, collectively hereinafter referred to as the Agricultural Universities (AUs).

Candidates having completed their Master’s degree program with a minimum of 55% marks or an OGPA of 5.5/10.00 or 2.75/5.00 or 2.20/4.00 or an equivalent OGPA from any recognized University in India and abroad would be eligible. For SC/ST and Physically Handicapped (PH) candidates, the minimum percentage of marks will be relaxed by 5 percent or an equivalent OGPA. The equivalence of OGPA to percent marks, where needed, will be certified by the Registrar of the concerned University. Candidates appearing in the final semester would also be eligible provided they complete their postgraduate degree in all respects by the date of examination and produce the complete degree certificate from the Registrar to this effect.

The fellowship would be granted only when the candidate gets eventually admitted and pursues a Ph.D. degree in an Agricultural University(AU) other than the Agricultural University(AU) from where the candidate has completed M.Sc./M.V.Sc./ M.E./M.Tech. degree.

The upper age limit would be 30 years as of the date of the examination. For SC/ST & PH categories, the upper age limit will be relaxed by 5 years. For OBC the upper age limit will be relaxed by 3 years. For in-service candidates of Agricultural Universities (AU), the upper age limit would be 45 years as of the date of examination whereas, the academic performance requirement would remain as stated above.

NOTE 1:

Reservation of various categories such as SC/ST/OBC and PH etc. will be given as per Government of India rules/instructions issued from time to time. The responsibility of verification of the genuineness of SC/ST/OBC and PH certificates will solely rest with the concerned Agricultural University (AU) where the candidate has been recommended for admission or granted provisional admission.

NOTE 2:

The ICAR-SRF (PGS) will NOT be available for admission in any university other than the AUs as mentioned above.

Application process

Online

Step 1:

Candidates need to aррly fоr Оnline Registrаtiоn by using a unique Emаil Id аnd Mоbile Nо.

Step 2:

Nоw, fill in the neсessаry detаils suсh аs Рersоnаl Detаils, Соntасt Detаils, Асаdemiс Quаlifiсаtiоns, etс.

Step 3:

Uрlоаd the required documents like the sсаnned рhоtоgrарh, signаture, аnd thumb imрressiоn аfter filling uр the detаils.

Step 4:

Nоw, Раy the Аррliсаtiоn Fees.

Step 5:

Аfter filling the аррliсаtiоn fоrm, саndidаtes will get the system generаted Аррliсаtiоn Number.

Step 6:

Оn соmрleting the аbоve рrосess аррliсаnts will hаve tо send the hаrd сорy оf the оnline аррliсаtiоn аnd рrооf оf fee раyment tо the СОE (Аgril. Edn.) by роst.

Application Correction

After submitting the application form for ICAR SRF candidates will get a chance to correct their mistakes. The NTA will provide a correction window to edit the application for the last time. With the help of credentials, candidates can update the application form and rectify their mistakes. No further chance will be given to candidates if they fail to correct their application in this window.

Required documents

Candidates must be ready with the following documents while filling out the Application form.

Candidate’s Photograph (file size: 10 kb - 200 kb)

Candidate’s Signature (file size: 4kb - 30kb)

Thumb impression (file size: 3kb-30kb)

Govt Identity Details like Aadhaar Number /Election Card (EPIC No.)/Passport number/Ration Card Number/ Bank Account Number/PAN Number/ Other valid Govt Ids.

Three identical copies of the latest passport-size colored photographs (with name and date)

Copy of payment of application fee (As proof)

Post-office receipt as postal dispatch proof of application.

Address for communication, Mobile Number, email id, etc

Bank Account details for payment of Fee, for uploading as part of the submission of the online application.

Note - The Thumb Impression used for filling the Online Application Form for ICAR, should be Left (for Males) and Right (for Females),

Frequently asked questions

Question: Does ICAR release the application forms for PhD courses?

Answer: The National Testing Agency (NTA) conducted ICAR AICE and ICAR AIEEA on behalf of ICAR. Candidates had to visit the official website of ICAR-NTA to apply online

Question: What are different modes to apply for SRF(PhD)]?

Answer: Application Forms can only be submitted online mode on the website https://icar.nta.ac.in. The Application Form other than online mode will not be accepted

Question: Can a person submit more than one application form for the exam

Answer: NO. Only ONE application is to be submitted by a candidate for appearing in the exam.

Question: What documents or certificates do I need to upload along with the Application Form

Answer: Candidates need to upload scanned images of their photograph, signature and thumb impression, with the Application Form. No certificates are required to be uploaded along with the Application Form at the time of online submission

Question: How can I pay Application Fee ?

Answer: Fee can be paid using SBI/Canara /HDFC/ICICI Bank Payment Gateway through Debit Card/Credit Card/Net Banking/UPI/Paytm. Candidates need to keep proof of fee paid.

Question: If I have made any mistake(s) while registering/applying, can I make changes later in the Application Form?

Answer: Once the ‘Final Submit’ button has been clicked, the candidate’s details cannot be edited/changed. However, NTA shall open the “Correction Window” as per the schedule and the Correction in particulars of the Application Form can be incorporated on the website only during the “Correction Window“. No corrections shall be allowed after the closure of the correction window and all particulars entered by the candidate would be considered as final.
